stances.claim: Ambassador Howard Q. Dee 'personified to the hilt' the twin beacons RVR Sr. stood for -- 'matchless excellence in business and extraordinary devotion to the less privileged' -- making him the rightful sole 2024 RVR awardee.

More than being a top business leader, Dee was 'God's servant first,' upholding the credo (to which CJ 'also humbly adhere[s]') that though it matters to have the things money can buy, 'it is far more important to have the things that money cannot buy like integrity, honor, truth, trustworthiness and an enduring love for, and abiding faith in, our God.'
stances.rhetorical_move: money-can-buy vs money-cannot-buy credo with personal-adherence disclosure

stances.claim: Dee pioneered the Philippine concept of corporate social responsibility -- co-founding PBSP in the early 1970s with Bienvenido A. Tan, persuading the top 50 tycoons to set aside 1% of net income before taxes for pro-poor programs; PBSP now has 230+ corporate members under Manuel V. Pangilinan.

Dee's most decisive contribution was founding and chairing ASA Philippines Foundation (July 1994), which in 2022 earned P5.9B, served 2M+ clients across 1,683 branches with 11,401 employees, and sustained a 'manageable repayment rate of 93.97 percent' -- defying the banking industry's avoidance of MSMEs.

FLP is launching a complementary 'Prosperity Fund' to 'invest in the equity of, and assist in managing, MSMEs to help the poor help themselves through private entrepreneurship' -- explicitly non-duplicative of ASA's microlending and (to CJ's knowledge) 'not being undertaken by any organization.'

Dee's life proves 'that the Filipino is trustworthy, credit-worthy, and Christ-worthy' -- a triadic vindication through demonstrated microfinance repayment, philanthropic faithfulness, and Christ-following service.

one_paragraph_summary: Ambassador Howard Q. Dee, 94, was proclaimed the sole recipient of the 2024 'RVR Award for Nation Building' on August 20. Moments after delivering his well-applauded acceptance speech and walking back to his seat adjacent to CJ's, he slumped; rushed to St. Luke's Global Medical Center, he died the next day on August 21, Ninoy Aquino Day. As chair of the RVR board of judges, CJ had explained why Dee was unanimously chosen, not realizing his address would become 'a virtual eulogy.' From heaven, the late Ambassador Ramon V. del Rosario Sr. 'must have been smiling' because Dee 'personified to the hilt the twin beacons that he stood for -- matchless excellence in business and extraordinary devotion to the less privileged.' Dee had a brilliant record as Unilab president and CEO, competing favorably with Roche, Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson, Novartis, and Merck. But 'more than being a top business leader, he was God's servant first,' upholding the credo (to which CJ also 'humbly adhere[s]') that though it is important to have what money can buy (food on the table, clothes on our back, a home for the family, and even a car), 'it is far more important to have the things that money cannot buy like integrity, honor, truth, trustworthiness and an enduring love for, and abiding faith in, our God.' Dee pioneered Philippine corporate social responsibility by inviting (with Bienvenido A. Tan) the top 50 tycoons in the early 1970s to form PBSP, with each setting aside 1% of net income before taxes; PBSP today has 230+ corporate members led by Manuel V. Pangilinan. After retiring from Unilab in 1970, Dee founded the Assisi Development Foundation to serve the poor 'just as our Lord Jesus Christ did, without any condition or expectation of reward'; later chaired the government peace panel with CPP-NPA-NDF (1993-1999); Cory Aquino named him ambassador to the Holy See and Malta; in 2018 he received the Ramon Magsaysay Award. What most impressed the board was his founding and chairship of ASA Philippines Foundation (July 1994), lending small sums to the poor: by 2022 it had earned P5.9 billion, served 2M+ clients across 1,683 branches with 11,401 employees, sustaining a 'manageable repayment rate of 93.97 percent' -- defying the banking industry's avoidance of MSMEs. As an aside, CJ announces FLP is launching a 'Prosperity Fund' -- equity investment in and management assistance to MSMEs, 'to help the poor help themselves through private entrepreneurship' -- explicitly non-duplicative of ASA's microlending and (to CJ's knowledge) 'not being undertaken by any organization.' Co-chairs are Amando M. Tetangco Jr. and Estela M. Perlas-Bernabe. For showing 'that the Filipino is trustworthy, credit-worthy, and Christ-worthy,' Dee fully deserves the RVR Award. CJ preserves the full board roster (Bacani, Cuisia, Gosingtian, Kang, Pangilinan, Ramon R. del Rosario Jr., Victor J. del Rosario, Tambunting) and closes: 'Thank you, Ambassador Howard Q. Dee, for your enduring legacy. To God be the glory!'
